definitions: Horace Greeley (1811-1872) was an American newspaper editor and publisher who founded the New York Tribune.
He was also a prominent politician, serving as a U.S. Representative from New York and as a presidential candidate for the Liberal Republican Party in 1872.
examples: Horace Greeley famously advised, "Go West, young man."
The New York Tribune under Horace Greeley was a powerful voice in American journalism.
